wall_name: Stock/B-roll library footage (not Eco's apartment) - mixed English technical/reference and Chinese biographical series
notes: Wide-angle B-roll of a large modern reference library, not Eco's Milan apartment; included because shelves and legible spines are visible. Spines mostly technical/corporate reference works (engineering, mathematics, chemistry) plus an Encyclopaedia Judaica run and, further along the same shelf (see t_011310), a Chinese-language biographical series.

wall_name: Artistic miniature diorama (shadow-box) of a library/study with fireplace and framed Eco portraits, shown in the film's Epilogo segment - not a real full-size shelf
notes: Miniature (dollhouse-scale) recreation of a book-lined fireplace nook, appearing repeatedly as static B-roll during the film's Epilogo title card; tiny printed book-spine facsimiles are mostly illegible at this scale even at 2x/3x crop. Only 'Stendhal' (blue spine, row 3) and a partial 'ARTE' (red spine) could be made out with confidence. Two framed photographs tucked into the shelves show Umberto Eco himself (different portraits).

wall_name: Real Milan apartment - long white Billy-style shelving corridor (a child on rollerblades visible in the aisle)
notes: Wide high-angle shot of the real corridor/library seen briefly during the Epilogo; camera is far from the shelves so almost all spines are too small to read even after 3x crop+sharpen. One title/author pair is legible on a white spine with black block lettering. A yellow-jacketed illustrated book lies flat with a title beginning 'LE ...' too blurred to read confidently (left unlabelled).

wall_name: Real Milan apartment, exterior courtyard shot through two open windows with flower boxes, shelving visible inside both rooms

books.title: Clave: diccionario de uso del español actual

notes: Establishing exterior shot (courtyard/light-well view) looking into two windows of the real apartment; camera is outdoors so most spines are too small even after 4x crop. A French 'Le Robert' dictionary volume and a Spanish 'Clave' dictionary are legible on the right-hand shelf; a run of ~10 uniform red-spine reference volumes (possibly an encyclopedia) sits alongside, titles not legible. Video cuts next to a girl on rollerblades skating away down a dim corridor (t_011436-t_011442), too dark to read any spines.

wall_name: Rare-book room, dark wood table with antique volumes
notes: Table-top shot in what is clearly Eco's rare-book/antiquarian room: a 17th-century volume lies open to its engraved title page reading ARS MAGNA SCIENDI (Kircher's 1669 combinatorial-logic treatise); a second closed vellum-bound volume sits behind it, title not visible from this angle.

notes: This shelf is a dedicated Athanasius Kircher collection (17th-century Jesuit polymath) - vellum and tooled-leather bindings, some with inset paper spine labels reading KIRCHERI / KIRCHERIA. A matching blue-and-gilt-tooled multi-volume set (visible edge-on through the cabinet glass at right) is Kircher's Obeliscus Aegyptiacus. s_011517_12.jpg is the same shelf, closer, no additional legible spines beyond these.
